description: Somos un equipo interdisciplinario que combina inteligencia artificial, desarrollo tecnológico, ingeniería química, biotecnología y relaciones internacionales para desarrollar soluciones innovadoras a desafíos globales, utilizando ciencia y datos para generar un impacto real.
summary: AgroFlow is a web platform that helps Argentine crop producers plan harvest operations and connect farms with transport, storage, and machinery services. It combines field location and area, crop and season information, historical weather context from NASA POWER, forecasts from Open-Meteo, and road routing from OpenStreetMap-based services to support harvest and logistics decisions. Producers can map their fields, explore planning scenarios, and request service quotes; providers manage their offerings and respond through role-specific workspaces. By bringing weather, timing, transport, storage, and service availability into one workflow, AgroFlow aims to reduce avoidable delays, improve coordination, and support more resilient and cost-aware harvest decisions. NASA POWER provides regional historical context—not field-level measurements—and the platform treats estimates and assumptions transparently rather than presenting them as certainty.
details:
AgroFlow brings harvest planning and agricultural service coordination together in one web application. Producers can create an account, register fields by drawing their boundaries on a map, and review planning information for their operations. The platform combines historical weather context from NASA POWER with forecasts from Open-Meteo. It also uses OpenStreetMap-based geocoding and road-routing services to help users locate places and estimate travel distances. Where available, agricultural yield information and port or market data can provide additional context; some port, price, capacity, and demonstration data is manually entered, simulated, or based on editable assumptions.

The application has separate workspaces for producers and service providers. Producers can browse transport, storage, and machinery offerings and request a quote. Providers can manage their service details, review incoming requests, and submit quotes. Contact information is shared as part of the accepted-quote workflow.

AgroFlow was built with React and JSX, Vite, and a Node.js API. Neon provides authentication and PostgreSQL storage, and Vercel hosts the web application and API functions. Interactive maps use MapLibre with OpenFreeMap/OpenStreetMap map data and an Esri imagery option. An optional AI explanation feature can use OpenAI; a template is available as a fallback.

The project’s creative approach is to connect weather, field context, logistics, and service availability instead of treating them as separate tools. The intended impact is better coordination and fewer avoidable delays, with the potential to reduce unnecessary travel and idle time. These benefits have not yet been measured. We considered data coverage and uncertainty, the difference between regional models and field observations, ease of mapping, privacy of user locations and contact details, and the need to identify simulated or assumed values. No custom hardware is currently deployed; sensor-based silo monitoring remains outside the live data workflow.
